page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 50 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory performance present notable bottlenecks. While small-block cached memory read bandwidth is average at 563.42 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to a poor 6.32 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU physics, and Redis SET operations also fall into the bottom 25%, reflecting the limitations of the shared CPU allocation and memory subsystem under heavy multi-threaded or memory-intensive workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a balanced resource density of vCPU and memory within a budget-friendly starter tier, making it a viable option for workloads that do not continuously saturate the CPU. The hardware supports advanced vector and cryptography instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AES, which assist in basic encryption and vector processing. Given the shared CPU model and the observed memory bandwidth constraints on large blocks, this server is best suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, lightweight database operations, software compilation, and small-scale development or CI/CD tasks rather than high-performance computing or large-scale data processing.
